description: Cross-language conformance traces for stream-level frame DECODE: how a byte-oriented transport's reads become frames. Message-level encoding is golden.json's job and is not retested here. PHASE 1: every arm EMITS its own answers to frame-stream-trace.<arm>.json and asserts nothing. Diff those files; each difference is a spec question nobody has answered. Once reconciled, freeze the agreed answers and flip every runner to assert. The two Rust endecs are separate arms because they already disagree on resync, which is the whole reason this corpus exists.

arms.rust-bridge: crates/lib/src/protocol/endec.rs WireEndec as a tokio_util Decoder, typed to GatewayToBridgeMsg (the BridgeEndec alias, daemon side) - resyncs past bad magic, bad version and an over-cap length by scanning for the next magic; coerces unknown compression and encoding bytes to none/msgpack.
arms.rust-gateway: the same WireEndec state machine typed to BridgeToGatewayMsg (the GatewayEndec alias, companion side). A separate arm because the two decoders disagreed on resync when this corpus was captured; they are one implementation now.
arms.swift: packages/gateway/swift FrameAccumulator composed with Codec.decode, the pairing Gateway.swift uses - the accumulator throws on bad magic, bad version, unknown compression, unknown encoding and a payload over 8 MiB, and never resyncs.
arms.kotlin: packages/gateway/kotlin FrameAccumulator composed with Codec.decode, the pairing Gateway.kt uses - same rejection set as swift, but the length cap compares a signed Long.

skipped_arms.webapp-shared-push: packages/webapp-shared/src/push.ts carries a sixth private accumulator, but it is a developer script's inbound reader that only ever speaks to a local daemon socket, rejects compression outright, and is not part of any SDK surface. Capturing it would produce divergences nobody intends to reconcile.

header.layout: magic u16 BE 0xdead | version u8 | compression u8 | encoding u8 | priority u8 | reserved 2 | length u64 BE (post-compression payload bytes)

payloads.note: Every payload in every case is a WireError-variant wire message. That variant exists in both directions with an identical serde shape, so the same bytes typed-decode as GatewayToBridgeMsg and as BridgeToGatewayMsg, which is what lets all four arms report the same frame identity. Bytes were produced by a msgpack writer verified byte-identical to rmp_serde to_vec_named against golden.json's error fixtures, and golden.rs already asserts those shapes re-encode byte-stably, so a Rust arm may recover payload bytes by re-encoding the message it decoded.
payloads.provenance: each payload is golden.json's error fixture shape with the id patched and the reason string resized: map3 { id: bin8/16, meta: map2 { kind: "response", data: map1 { requestId: bin8/16 } }, data: map2 { type: "error", data: <WireError> } }, WireError being map1 { type: "unsupported" } or map2 { type: "handlerFailed"|"malformed", data: map1 { reason: str } }. ids differ only in their final byte so payload length is unaffected. gzip bodies are level 6 with mtime 0. no payload contains the byte pair de ad, so a resync scan can never land inside one. to add a case, follow the same layout: the corpus is a frozen data artifact and is deliberately not generated by a checked-in second msgpack encoder.

contract.drive: for each case: create a fresh decoder, then for each chunk length in `chunks` in order, feed exactly that many bytes from `stream_hex` (a length of 0 means feed an empty buffer) and then drain: call the decoder repeatedly until it yields nothing more, appending one event per frame and one event per error.
contract.errors: an error never ends the case by itself. record it and keep draining, then keep feeding chunks. the harness applies no recovery of its own: it never resets, reallocates or drops the decoder, so whatever the implementation left buffered is what the next call sees.
contract.stall: if a drain iteration produces an error and the decoder's buffered byte count is unchanged from immediately before that iteration, the stream cannot progress: record the event, stop draining, feed no further chunks, and set terminal.state to `stalled`. a hard cap of 64 events per case is the backstop.
contract.crash: some cases can trap or panic an arm rather than returning an error. wrap each case in the language's catch-all (catch_unwind in Rust), record terminal.state `panicked` with whatever events were produced first, and carry on with the next case. a case that crashes an arm is an answer, not a capture failure.
contract.seam: the seam is the full decode path: framing plus decompression plus typed decode. the Rust arms are that already; the Swift and Kotlin arms compose FrameAccumulator with Codec.decode exactly as their Gateway does, and report an accumulator throw and a Codec throw as different error kinds.
contract.payload_identity: payload_sha256 and payload_len are over the DECOMPRESSED payload, so a gzip frame and a plain frame carrying the same message report the same values. arms that consume the bytes during typed decode recover them by re-encoding the decoded message.
contract.clock: none. nothing in this corpus is timed and no arm may report wall-clock values.

emitted.file: crates/lib/fixtures/frame-stream-trace.<arm>.json, arm one of the keys in "arms".
emitted.shape: { "impl": "<arm>", "constants": {...}, "unobserved": [...], "notes": "...", "cases": [ { "name": ..., "steps": [...], "terminal": {...} } ] }. one step per event the arm produced, in order; the arm's own step count is an answer, so do not pad to match another arm.

step_fields.after_chunk: 0-based index of the chunk whose drain produced this event.
step_fields.consumed_bytes: total stream bytes the decoder has taken in at this point: bytes fed so far minus bytes still buffered. this is how a resync is measured, since no arm reports skipping directly.
step_fields.priority: "normal", "bulk" or "background" on a frame, null on an error.
step_fields.compression: "none" or "gzip" on a frame, null on an error. Rust arms cannot see this through the Decoder trait and declare it unobserved.
step_fields.encoding: "msgpack" or "json" on a frame, null on an error. same unobservability as compression.
step_fields.payload_len: decompressed payload byte count on a frame, null on an error.
step_fields.payload_sha256: lowercase hex sha256 of the decompressed payload on a frame, null on an error. cross-check it against payloads.table.
step_fields.frame_id: lowercase hyphenated uuid from the decoded message's id field on a frame, null on an error.
step_fields.error_kind: on an error, one of: invalid_magic, unsupported_version, unsupported_compression, unsupported_encoding, payload_too_large, header_too_short, payload_too_short, decompress_failed, typed_decode_failed, other. null on a frame. an arm that has to reach for `other` records the raw type it mapped from in the file's top-level notes, not in the step.
step_fields.error_stage: on an error, "framing", "decompress" or "typed": which stage of the seam raised it. null on a frame.
step_fields.recoverable: on an error, what the arm's own API says about recoverability (EndecError::is_recoverable in Rust), or null where the API has no such notion. null on a frame.

terminal_fields.state: "ok" when every chunk was fed and nothing is left buffered, "incomplete" when every chunk was fed and bytes remain, "stalled" when the no-progress rule stopped the run, "panicked" when the arm trapped.
terminal_fields.buffered_bytes: bytes the decoder still holds at the end of the case.
terminal_fields.consumed_bytes: total stream bytes consumed over the whole case.

constants.header_len: 16 everywhere; an arm that says otherwise has found something.
constants.max_payload_bytes: the arm's declared payload ceiling, or null when it has none.
constants.resyncs_past_bad_magic: whether the arm scans forward for the next magic instead of failing the stream.
constants.rejects_unknown_compression: whether an unrecognised compression byte is an error rather than a coercion to none.
constants.rejects_unknown_encoding: the same question for the encoding byte.
constants.decodes_typed_payload: whether the seam under capture includes typed decode.
constants.auto_gzip_threshold_bytes: the arm's encoder-side auto-gzip threshold, or null where it has none. informational: it is why the corpus has cases at 16255, 16256 and 16257, and it is not exercised by decode.

emitted.unobserved: top-level array of step field names this arm structurally cannot answer, so the differ skips them for it rather than reading a null as a disagreement. rust-bridge and rust-gateway declare ["compression", "encoding"]. never use it to hide a field an arm simply did not implement.

cases.name: byte-at-a-time
cases.description: the same frame fed one byte per read; every intermediate state must yield nothing and lose nothing.

cases.name: empty-reads-around-a-frame
cases.description: zero-length reads interleaved with real ones; an empty read must be a no-op, not a decode attempt.

cases.name: only-empty-reads
cases.description: nothing but zero-length reads on an empty stream.

cases.name: three-frames-in-one-read
cases.description: three back-to-back frames delivered in a single read; the drain loop must pop all three.

cases.name: three-frames-split-inside-the-second-header
cases.description: read boundary lands 8 bytes into the second frame's header, after the first frame was already popped.

cases.name: three-frames-split-inside-the-second-body
cases.description: read boundary lands 40 bytes into the second frame's body.

cases.name: two-frames-byte-at-a-time
cases.description: two back-to-back frames fed one byte per read.

cases.name: mixed-priority-frames
cases.description: normal, bulk, background and an unknown priority byte 0x07 in one read; unknown priorities decode as normal.

cases.name: nonzero-reserved-bytes
cases.description: reserved bytes 6..8 carry 0xbeef; decoders must ignore them.

cases.name: bad-magic-mid-stream-then-valid-frame
cases.description: a good frame, 8 bytes of junk carrying no magic, then a good frame; the ratified behavior is to resync and decode both.

cases.name: leading-garbage-then-valid-frame
cases.description: junk before the first frame, including a lone 0xde that is not a frame start.

cases.name: magic-straddling-a-read-boundary-in-garbage
cases.description: the junk run ends on 0xde and the next read supplies the byte that decides it is not a frame start; a resyncing decoder must not discard the held byte.

cases.name: bad-magic-with-no-valid-frame-after
cases.description: 32 bytes of junk containing no magic and nothing after it.

cases.name: lone-magic-high-byte-at-end-of-stream
cases.description: the stream ends on a single 0xde; there is not enough left to decide whether it starts a frame.

cases.name: unsupported-version-then-valid-frame
cases.description: a frame claiming wire version 3, followed by a good version-2 frame.

cases.name: unknown-compression-byte-then-valid-frame
cases.description: compression byte 0x07 on an otherwise-good frame, followed by a good frame; Rust coerces unknown to none, the mobile accumulators reject.

cases.name: unknown-encoding-byte-then-valid-frame
cases.description: encoding byte 0x09 on an otherwise-good frame, followed by a good frame; Rust coerces unknown to msgpack, the mobile accumulators reject.

cases.name: truncated-final-frame-mid-header
cases.description: one good frame then 9 bytes of a second frame's header and nothing more.

cases.name: truncated-final-frame-mid-body
cases.description: one good frame then a complete second header with only 40 of its body bytes.

cases.name: truncated-only-frame
cases.description: a single frame cut off 56 bytes in; nothing is ever completable.

cases.name: zero-length-frame-then-valid-frame
cases.description: a well-formed header declaring a zero-byte payload, then a good frame; this is the shape the pre-2026-07-09 straddle bug fabricated out of a split header.

cases.name: length-above-the-mobile-cap-below-the-rust-cap-then-valid-frame
cases.description: a header declaring 12 MiB: over the 8 MiB mobile accumulator cap, under the 16 MiB Rust cap, 8 body bytes, then a good frame.

cases.name: length-just-over-the-rust-cap-then-valid-frame
cases.description: a header declaring 16 MiB + 1: over every cap, still a plausible u64, 8 body bytes, then a good frame.

cases.name: length-two-to-the-sixty-third-then-valid-frame
cases.description: a header declaring 2^63: absurd but does not overflow a usize when the header length is added, 8 body bytes, then a good frame.

cases.name: length-u64-max-then-valid-frame
cases.description: a header declaring u64::MAX: header length plus payload length overflows a 64-bit size, 8 body bytes, then a good frame.

cases.name: gzip-frame-decompressing-to-16255
cases.description: a gzip frame whose decompressed payload is 16255 bytes, one below / at / one above the 16256-byte auto-gzip threshold senders use.

cases.name: gzip-frame-decompressing-to-16256
cases.description: a gzip frame whose decompressed payload is 16256 bytes, one below / at / one above the 16256-byte auto-gzip threshold senders use.

cases.name: gzip-frame-decompressing-to-16257
cases.description: a gzip frame whose decompressed payload is 16257 bytes, one below / at / one above the 16256-byte auto-gzip threshold senders use.

cases.name: gzip-frame-split-mid-body
cases.description: the threshold-sized gzip frame cut in the middle of its compressed body.

cases.name: gzip-and-plain-frames-interleaved
cases.description: plain, gzip, plain in one read; the length field is the post-compression byte count in every case.

cases.name: gzip-frame-with-corrupt-deflate-then-valid-frame
cases.description: a gzip frame whose deflate stream is damaged, then a good frame; framing is intact, only inflation fails.

cases.name: large-uncompressed-frame-in-1024-byte-reads
cases.description: a 16256-byte uncompressed payload delivered in 1 KiB reads; exercises buffer growth and multi-read body reassembly.

cases.name: valid-framing-invalid-payload-then-valid-frame
cases.description: a frame whose 3-byte body is not decodable msgpack, then a good frame; framing never desyncs, so the good frame must still arrive.
